rationale: Block 3 covers clinical presentation including the characteristic indolent onset — distinguishing TB from pyogenic infection is a core OR4.1 trap.

Block 4 covers pathology and mechanism — Pott's disease affects the lower thoracic/thoracolumbar junction, cold abscess tracking, and gibbus formation. This question tests the classic location and complication pattern.

Block 7 covers management including the ATT regimen (2HRZE/4HR) and the indication for surgery — anterior debridement (Hodgson procedure) NOT posterior laminectomy. This is a high-yield surgical trap.

Block 6 covers investigations — FNAC/biopsy for diagnosis and the characteristic radiological finding of preserved joint space in early TB hip (cartilage is destroyed late, unlike pyogenic arthritis).
